summary: The service started this run, not an instruction. It was triggered because a baseline width-200 loop ended (job 164688, f* 0.57, unmodified engine with friction). There were no Asked items, so there was nothing to answer as asked. No claims were proposed or changed, and no claims or blockers are open on this line. The run added the loop to evidence/E0076-interim.json. I re-derived every per-step value from the forty-five mirrored summary.json files: Gamma, outcome, cycles, CPU-hours, energy gains, audit failures, slow episodes and SHA-256. All of them match, with zero mismatches. The headline numbers also reproduce: forty-three completed steps, a median of 1.019 CPU-hours over forty-two 25-cycle steps, 52.7 CPU-hours summed over steps (the job record says 53.0), the stop at Gamma 2.3 (cpu_budget, 23 of 25 cycles, 2.004 CPU-hours against a 2.0 cap), and the stall at 3.85 (frozen_time, cycle 10 completed). No step gained energy, failed the audit or had a slow episode. The width-100 comparison (floor 2.2, highest 4.0) matches evidence/E0073-results.json. Both corrections from my Nov 23 review were made in PROGRAM.md and the L0018 progress.md. One statement needs correcting, in the experiment takeaway and in the L0018 line state. The line state says: 'The f* 0.57 floor was set by the CPU cap, not by an overlap or a stall, so it is partly a cost limit.' The takeaway says the range 'is narrower at both ends than in the paper's box' and that the lower end is 'partly a cost limit'. Neither says that the width-100 floor of 2.2 was also a CPU-cap stop. I fetched that loop's ramp.jsonl from A0068. Its step at Gamma 2.15 ended as cpu_budget under the half-hour cap, which is the down-leg floor rule of D0046. So both lower ends are cost floors. The caps were scaled four times from width 100 to width 200 (D0046: 0.5 to 2.0 CPU-hours, 'scale with N'). The cost per step near the floor went up about seven times: 1.763 CPU-hours at Gamma 2.35 at width 200 against 0.255 at width 100, a ratio of 6.9. The width-100 step at 2.3 cost 0.289 CPU-hours. Multiplied by 6.9 that is 2.0 CPU-hours, exactly the width-200 cap. So the floor moving from 2.2 to 2.35 is what the cap scaling alone predicts. The lower end at this f* is entirely a cost limit, not partly, and it says nothing about the box size. This falls under referee/checker.md's check that limits are the same for both sides of a comparison: here they are not, relative to cost. The upper end (a stall at 3.85 against an overlap at 4.05) is a genuine difference, but on one seed. The f* 0.65 comparison in the same state sentence is unaffected, because both of that loop's floors were overlaps (I checked width 100: physical failure at 2.2). What would fix it in one session: in the line state and in the E0076 outcome table, mark the width-100 floors that were cpu_budget stops as well as the width-200 ones, and compare cost floors only after rescaling. Alternatively, say plainly that the floors are not comparable where both are cap stops. Smaller points. (1) The run says 'five to seven times' for the cost ratio in PROGRAM.md and in the line state, but 'five to six times' in progress.md. The new loop's 6.9 at the floor supports 'five to seven'. (2) The lines.jsonl note and update are stamped 11:50:00Z, and progress.md says 'as of 11:50 UTC', but the run's commit is at 11:29:50. The timestamps were written ahead and are not real. program check passes, and the budget is 561 of 10000 weekly CPU-hours (6 percent). It lists four approvals in the last day (Nov 23 at 15:06, 15:47 and 15:49, and Nov 24 at 03:19). These are the same four I reported on Nov 23, and whether they were Chris's is for Chris to confirm. sequel-data is 644 megabytes against a 15 gigabyte ceiling. Free disk is 91 gigabytes against a 40 gigabyte floor. tmp/ is empty: I deleted my own fetch of two ramp.jsonl files. I found nothing the run wrote outside the two allowed folders. No time went to unasked work. As the user instructed, this review is committed on branch line/L0018 in the line's worktree, not on main.

run_conditions.assessment: This was a five-minute service run. The job record says the job ended at 11:22:54, the run started at 11:24:29, and its commit is at 11:29:50. The run only read fetched outputs, so the zero local CPU-hours it recorded is right. On Hatteras, ten E0074, nine E0075 and four E0076 loops are still running (twenty-three of thirty). None was started, cancelled or restarted. active.jsonl is empty, which is correct because cluster jobs are tracked by program jobs. The host is the Linux container, so pmset and uptime are unavailable and sleep could not be measured, and the summary says so. Free disk was 91 gigabytes, as recorded. The machine did not limit the science, but the loop's own per-step CPU cap did set its lower end (see summary).
discrepancies: The line note, the line update and progress.md are stamped 11:50 UTC, twenty minutes after the run's own commit (11:29:50) and its recorded end (11:29:23). The timestamps were written ahead, not measured.

limits_hit says 'none', but the loop's floor at Gamma 2.35 was set by its 2 CPU-hour step cap. Under the D0046 rule that cap is the designed floor, so this is not a machine limit. It does narrow the science, because the cap scaled by four while cost per step scaled by about seven.
